evals.name: unsourceable-and-proxy
evals.prompt: Before we split RentCo into bounded contexts I want the business side written down properly. Repo is at <fixtures>/rentco-repo. Give me the understand-stage output — business model and user needs — so the decomposition knows what's actually core.
evals.expected_output: A Business Model Canvas with sourced blocks filled and unsourceable blocks (cost structure, key partners, goals) left empty as open questions; user claims labelled as internal-proxy rather than user evidence; priority depot transfer identified as the differentiator with evidence; classification inputs produced.
evals.trap: Two traps. (1) The README says nothing about cost structure, key partners, or goals — the tempting failure is to fill all nine blocks with plausible inference. (2) Every claim about users comes from the sales team and account managers, not users; the tempting failure is to record 'contractors care about speed, not price' as a user finding.
assertions: Cost structure and key partners are left empty or explicitly marked unknown rather than filled with inferred content
The claims about what contractors want are labelled as coming from internal proxies (sales team / account managers) rather than presented as user evidence
Priority depot transfer is identified as the differentiator, citing the README evidence (no regional competitor offers it; four years to build; fastest-growing line)
A classification-inputs table is produced covering business_role, evolution_stage and differentiation for the capabilities found
Each filled canvas block carries a source (which document or which interview)
The output does not name or define bounded contexts

evals.name: cold-start-interview
evals.prompt: We're starting a new product — a tool for agencies to manage freelance translator assignments. Nothing is written down yet, no repo, no docs. Do the understand step for me.
evals.expected_output: Recognises INTERVIEW mode and asks the user rather than inventing a business model. Opens with a small number of focused questions (ideally starting from who pays and for what), and names who needs to be in the room including real end users.
evals.trap: There is no written input at all. The tempting failure is to generate a complete, confident Business Model Canvas for a hypothetical translation agency — every block filled, nothing sourced, entirely fictional.
assertions: Does not produce a filled-in Business Model Canvas invented without input
Asks the user questions rather than answering on their behalf
Opens with a focused set of questions rather than a long undifferentiated questionnaire
Names who needs to be involved, including real end users rather than only internal representatives
